forge-mat.basis: 183 cm³ × 0.00785 kg/cm³ (steel, confirmed by engineer); steel → 38MnVS6 (Microalloyed) (representative forging billet — not a drawing callout)

forge-part-wt.basis: 1.433 kg finished + 22.8 cm³ of holes drilled from solid (≤ Ø25; larger bores pierced) + 81.5 cm³ machining stock (2.5 mm a side on the machined faces — IS 3469 (Part I):1974 Table 1.5 minimum finish stock for a drop / press forging whose greatest dimension (250.0 mm) is over 205 mm and not over 410 mm) + 8.2 cm³ turning stock on the 41 cm² turned axis (2 mm a side, engineering-typical, not sourced) + 0.0 cm³ draft metal (no zero-draft forged face along the Z parting axis — no draft metal) = 1.433 kg + 112.5 cm³ × 0.00785 kg/cm³ = 2.316 kg — 183 cm³ × 0.00785 kg/cm³ (steel, confirmed by engineer)

forge-proj-area.basis: largest of the three measured silhouettes — a forging parts round its largest periphery

forge-shape.basis: score 0 + 0 + 0 = 0 → simple — 0 for 0 free-form face(s), 0 for 2 undercut face(s), 0 for 50 faces (≥ 3 complex, ≥ 1 moderate; free-form ≥ 3 / ≥ 8, undercuts ≥ 4, faces ≥ 120 — CostVision heuristic)

forge-yield.basis: closed-die stock yield band 0.55–0.8, midpoint 0.675 — as-forged weight ÷ billet, CostVision engineering-typical, not sourced; the 10% flash is itemised, so yieldFraction = 0.675 × 1.10 = 0.743; billet = 2.316 kg forging + 0.232 kg flash = 2.548 kg ÷ 0.743 = 3.429 kg; finished ÷ billet = 1.433 kg ÷ 3.429 kg = 0.42; 3.429 − 2.548 = 0.881 kg is scale, crop and any pierced wad (not itemised)

forge-flash.basis: 10% of the 2.316 kg forging, squeezed out at the flash land (CostVision engineering-typical, not sourced) — cost-neutral: the yield is scaled by the same fraction, so the billet stays forging ÷ 0.675

forge-mach.basis: Kt 3 for a simple shape, σflow 105 MPa hot flow stress for microalloyed-steel (both CostVision engineering-typical, not sourced); A = 84.3 cm² silhouette + 16.69 cm² flash land = 100.99 cm²; F = Kt × σflow × A = 3 × 105 MPa × 10,099 mm² ÷ 9,806.65 N/t = 324 t × 1.2 safety = 389 t → the smallest forge press at or above it: the 500 t press (library presses 500, 1,600, 2,500, 4,000, 8,000 t)

forge-strokes.basis: 2 hit(s): 2 impression(s); takt = 3 s billet from the heater + 2 × 4 s mechanical press hit + transfer = 11 s (load and hit times CostVision engineering-typical, not sourced)

forge-time-per-blow.basis: hit + transfer on the press (informational — the cycle below is the line takt)

forge-ct.basis: 2 hit(s): 2 impression(s); takt = 3 s billet from the heater + 2 × 4 s mechanical press hit + transfer = 11 s (load and hit times CostVision engineering-typical, not sourced). The billet cut-off and the induction heater are their own operations (billetSaw…, billetHeater…)

forge-manning.basis: closed-die line crew: forger + heater / handler — engineering typical

forge-reject.basis: 2% forging scrap (laps, underfill, cracks at inspection) — engineering typical

forge-furnace.basis: steel / titanium billets for an impression line heat in-line by induction

forge-saw-mach.basis: billet cut off the bar on the automatic carbide saw (billet 3.429 kg cut from round bar at a height / diameter of 2.3 (the free-upset limit, CostVision heuristic) = Ø62.3 mm; kerf π/4 × 62.3² mm² × 3 mm (engineering-typical carbide kerf, not sourced) × 7.85 g/cm³ = 0.0718 kg)

forge-saw-ct.basis: 1 ÷ 400 cuts an hour = 0.0025 h a billet — ENGINEERING ESTIMATE (no published cut time for this bar was found)

forge-saw-manning.basis: one operator tends two automatic saws — ENGINEERING ESTIMATE, not sourced

forge-saw-kerf.basis: billet 3.429 kg cut from round bar at a height / diameter of 2.3 (the free-upset limit, CostVision heuristic) = Ø62.3 mm; kerf π/4 × 62.3² mm² × 3 mm (engineering-typical carbide kerf, not sourced) × 7.85 g/cm³ = 0.0718 kg — bought as bar, lost in the cut, credited as scrap

forge-heater-mach.basis: the in-line induction billet heater (~500 kW, SMS Elotherm sizing); fed by the forge crew — no crew of its own; its energy is the per-kg heating line, not in its machine rate

forge-heater-ct.basis: 3.429 kg billet ÷ 1,250 kg/h = 0.00274 h a billet — the heater's throughput, SMS Elotherm (~500 kW to 1,250 °C, a maker's claim for billets ≤ Ø51 mm; a larger billet heats slower — not adjusted)

forge-trim-mach.basis: flash line 4.4 √A = 404 mm and flash 0.015 √A = 1.38 mm over A = 8,430 mm² (outline and thickness after ASM closed-die practice); 404 mm × 1.38 mm × 105 MPa hot flow stress ÷ 9,806.65 N/t = 6.0 t × 1.25 margin = 7.50 t → the 100 t press, the smallest mechanical press in the library at or above it (flow stress CostVision engineering-typical, not sourced; a pierce in the same stroke is not added to the force)

forge-trim-ct.basis: the trim press stands in line and works to the forge takt (11 s)

forge-trim-manning.basis: one operator on the in-line trim press

forge-die-cost.basis: 2-impression h13 die over 84.3 cm²: Die design & CAM 39 h £2,276 + Die blocks (both halves + holder allowance) 117 kg £1,107 + Block prep (squaring, faces, keyways) 35.8 h £1,876 + Die sinking × 2 impression(s) 126.4 h £6,621 + EDM (deep ribs, tight radii) 25.3 h £1,477 + Harden + temper the blocks £2,756 + Impression polishing × 2 25.6 h £1,160 + Die tryout — 3 sessions 18 h £1,541 = £18,814; toolmaker overhead + profit at 22% of it = £4,139; die set £18,814 + £4,139 = £22,953 (toolroom hours and the die-block rules are CostVision engineering-typical, not sourced; rates from the toolroom book)

forge-die-life.basis: size factor 1 (plan ≤ 100 cm²); 38,000 forgings a die set for microalloyed steel × 1.3 simple impression × 1.000000 size = 49,400 forgings — CostVision engineering-typical figures, not sourced; die sets are charged fractionally over the programme

forge-heat-energy.basis: energy to bring microalloyed-steel to forging temperature in the in-line induction heater: 500 kW ÷ 1,250 kg/h = 0.4 kWh/kg (SMS Elotherm, a maker's claim for steel billets ≤ Ø51 mm to 1,250 °C); charged on every billet heated: 0.4 kWh/kg × 3.429 kg billet ÷ 0.98 for the 2% scrap = 1.400 kWh a good part, priced at the costing book's tariff as kWh (gas furnace × 2.4 kWh of gas)

forge-ht-cost.basis: none — a microalloyed-steel forging is controlled-cooled from the forge heat (no separate heat treatment)

forge-descale.basis: forge scale removed after the trim, before MPI and machining (shot blast or pickle): £0.12/kg × the 2.316 kg forging — the flash is off by then — UK price × the country's process-service factor, CostVision engineering-typical, not sourced

forge-ndt.basis: 100% magnetic-particle inspection on a safety-critical closed-die forging, as a station: 75 s a part × (inspector £28.03/h × 1 + bench £4.00/h) = £0.67 a part — the casting route's MPI station (75 s and the bench engineering-typical, not sourced)

forge-sf-route.basis: not asked yet — costed bare (answer "Is the part coated?" to price a finish)

forge-sf-area.basis: measured surface 453.6 cm² = 0.0454 m² — the whole wetted surface; a masked or machined-after-coating face is in it
